title: [1] Create praxis-offline-codex.md
why_we_need_this:
You are working with github and development here. You're able to write code and make prs

You must read @praxis-mcp-codex.md 

Agents in our projects are not able to connect to praxis MCP, that's why we need to have working offline version of this instruction. We must save the process with which we're working. So any AI agent will go to project will read praxis-offline-codex.md and will get all the instructions with proper actions and will work better.

Also for the refere - you are able to look into .praxis/api/ with the code we've used with praxis-mcp-codex.md before.

I'm expecting from you Pull Request with the file praxis-offline-codex.md.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Full mapping of all 14 MCP tools to offline file-based commands:
   - Tasks: get_active_tasks, list_tasks, get_task, find_task_by_keywords, create_task, get_next_task_id, update_task, update_task_status
   - Assignees: get_assignees, find_assignee_by_keywords, create_assignee
   - Project Context: search_project_context, read_context_route, update_project_context
   - Settings: get_settings, update_settings
   Each MCP tool must have a clearly described offline equivalent using direct file operations (cat, read, write, move).

2. Step-by-step task execution workflow: read task → study project context → move to in_progress → execute → update task (what was done, what was not) → move to to_review → create PR. Each step must use offline file commands instead of MCP calls.

3. Search procedure for project-context: word-by-word search across all .md files inside project-context/ recursively. The codex must describe the search steps the agent should follow.

4. Task JSON schema documentation: example of a valid task JSON with all required fields (id, assignee, priority, status, title, why_we_need_this, acceptance_criteria, important_constraints, labels, on_hold_reason, created_at, column_entered_at). Document allowed values for priority (low, medium, high, critical) and status (new, in_progress, to_review, completed, on_hold, archived, error).

5. Task counter procedure: describe that task_counter file must be read, incremented by 1, and written back manually when creating a new task.

6. Ad-hoc request handling: if a user request is not related to any existing task, the agent must either create a new task for it or execute it directly, following the same workflow.

7. The file must be fully self-contained: an agent reads ONLY praxis-offline-codex.md and nothing else to understand how to work with Praxis.
important_constraints:
1. Safe file writes: always write to a temp file first, then rename/move to the target path to avoid corruption.

2. The document is written for AI agents, not humans. Language and structure must be optimized for agent consumption.

3. Status changes must be implemented as file moves between status directories (e.g. tasks/new/ → tasks/in_progress/) AND the status field inside the JSON must be updated to match.

4. Task counter is managed manually: read the current value, increment by 1, write back. Describe the file location and format.
